source_summary: Queried 6 GitHub Search API surfaces saved under /tmp/radar_2026_10_02_api/ for recently created and recently pushed AI agent, MCP, computer-use, browser automation, coding-agent, RAG/workflow, email, and spreadsheet-agent repositories. Shortlisted repository metadata, root contents, and README audits were saved under /tmp/radar_2026_10_02_readmes/. GitHub unauthenticated API later returned 403 rate limit, so Top projects primarily use complete audits while a few Watchlist entries are search-metadata-only.
trend_observations: Agent execution substrate continues to split into durable personal-agent brains, desktop/background agents, governed MCP/LLM gateways, multi-agent terminal workspaces, shared coding-agent memory, and narrow office-object MCP surfaces. The strongest candidates make tool calls, permissions, review, audit logs, rollback, long-term state, or local files into explicit product objects instead of only adding another prompt or skill collection. Email and spreadsheet tools are becoming serious agent product surfaces because they convert risky everyday objects into reviewable CLI/MCP contracts.
assumptions: Scores use GitHub metadata, repository descriptions/topics, root-content and README evidence, install/test/CI/security/download/example signals, created_at/pushed_at timing, and product-surface clarity. No third-party repository was cloned, installed, built, run, browser-tested, desktop-tested, Windows-tested, mobile-tested, MCP-connected, credential-tested, provider-tested, security-tested, payment-tested, or deployed locally. Star counts and pushed_at values are point-in-time metadata from the discovery window and can change quickly. GitHub API rate limiting prevented full audits for some late shortlist candidates; those are called out conservatively.
markdown_report: See data/runs/2026-10-02.md for the complete human-readable report. Top themes: personal-agent scale, open desktop dots, MCP/LLM governance, multi-agent terminal workspaces, cross-agent memory, Excel/email MCP surfaces, and VM-isolated coding-agent queues.
